bib.title: Generalizable Chain-of-Thought Prompting in Mixed-task Scenarios with Large Language Models

question: How can CoT prompting be both general and strong when incoming questions come from mixed, unknown task types in arbitrary order?
hypothesis: Routing each question to demonstrations of a matched type (and auto-building demos for unmatched types) closes the gap between zero-shot generality and few-shot performance.
contributions: Pioneer the setting of mixed-task scenarios
Propose GeM-CoT, a generalizable CoT prompting mechanism for mixed-task scenarios that improves performance while achieving generality
Experiments on 33 datasets show performance and generality

method.summary: GeM-CoT embeds the question with Sentence-BERT and matches it to the nearest demo in a typed demo pool by dot product; above a threshold it uses that type's demos for few-shot CoT, otherwise it runs Zero-Shot-CoT and caches the item. When the cache is large enough, OPTICS clusters it and large clusters yield 6 auto-built demos (k-means, Auto-CoT-style filtering) that join the pool.
method.task: chain-of-thought reasoning in mixed-task scenarios (arithmetic, commonsense, symbolic, BBH)

datasets.name: 10 reasoning datasets (AQuA, MultiArith, AddSub, GSM8K, SingleEq, SVAMP, Last Letter, Coin Flip, StrategyQA, CSQA)
datasets.size: AQuA 254, MultiArith 600, AddSub 395, GSM8K 1319, SingleEq 508, SVAMP 1000, CSQA 1221, StrategyQA 2290, Letter 500, Coin 500 (Table 7)
datasets.split: full test sets as sized in Table 7; basis of original demo pool

datasets.name: Pilot mixed set (Sec 3.2)
datasets.split: shuffled questions from the ten tasks
datasets.source: ten reasoning tasks following Kojima et al. 2023 and Zhang et al. 2023

inference.prompting: Few-shot CoT with type-matched demos formatted 'Q: q, A: r, a' then 'Q: q_in, A:'; unmatched path uses 'Let's think step by step.'
inference.retrieval: Nearest demo by dot product of Sentence-BERT embeddings; match if top score >= S_thres

parameters.clustering: OPTICS (density) then k-means within cluster, scikit-learn

other.Fig 4 streaming (read from Fig 4): batch size 400, five batches; accuracies in figure

baselines: General-CoT (one random demo per pool type as a generic prompt)
eval.protocol: Single runs reported; no seeds or significance tests stated.

prompts.purpose: LLM-based type classifier demos (alternative to Type Matching)
prompts.text:
Q: Was Aristotle a member of the House of Lords?
Type: <commonsense, yes-no>
prompts.where: Appendix C.3, Table 9 (six demos, one per category/form type)

prompts.text: A: Let's think step by step.

evidence.quote: The threshold numbers Sthres, thca and thcls are set to 0.35, 200 and 50 respectively.

results.claim: GeM-CoT averages 82.3% on ten reasoning datasets with GPT-3.5-Turbo, above Few-Shot-CoT (81.4) and Auto-CoT (82.1), which need known task type.
results.quote: GeM-CoT stands out by continually boosting the performance (i.e., 82.1%→82.3%)

results.claim: Generic-prompt CoT baselines lose accuracy versus Auto-CoT (82.1 to 79.4 for Zero-Shot-CoT, 80.7 for General-CoT).
results.quote: while the general CoT techniques both witness average performance degradation (i.e., 82.1%→79.4/80.7%)

results.claim: With GPT-4, GeM-CoT averages 86.6 over AQuA, GSM8K, SVAMP versus 85.5 Few-Shot-CoT and 81.0 Zero-Shot-CoT.
Pilot: Few-Shot-CoT with gold demos (known source) scores 78.0 versus 66.0 for Zero-Shot-CoT on a 100-question mixed sample.
results.setup: 100 shuffled questions from ten tasks, GPT-3.5-Turbo inferred from Sec 5.1
results.note: Backbone for the pilot is not stated in Sec 3.2.

results.claim: Naive few-shot with fixed single-dataset demos in mixed-task collapses to 27.0%.
Single-source demos beat mixed-source demos in the pilot (19.0/20.0 to 26.0/27.0).
results.note: Quote lists mixed then single; values 26.0/27.0 are single-source.

results.claim: Diversity-based demo selection beats similarity-based and random on AddSub (93.7 vs 90.1 and 92.2).
results.note: On StrategyQA similarity (64.1) and on AQuA random (52.0) are higher than GeM-CoT (63.5, 51.9).

results.claim: Replacing Type Matching with an LLM classifier gives comparable accuracy (93.4 AddSub, 64.5 Strategy) but costs API calls.
results.table: Table 6, row w/ classifier, column AddSub

results.claim: Gold-type oracle does not beat GeM-CoT on AddSub (90.1) but is higher on Strategy (65.0 vs 63.5).
results.table: Table 6, row w/ correct type, column AddSub

results.claim: An LLM asked to classify questions by task name with 10 demos is only 42% accurate; category+form typing reaches 99%.
results.note: 99% is read from Fig 10 axis labels (42, 80, 84, 99).

results.claim: Threshold 0.35 gave the best type-matching F1/accuracy over scores in [0.2, 0.6].
results.quote: choosing 0.35 yields the best results in general across our tasks

results.claim: On BBH streaming, GeM-CoT overtakes Zero-Shot-CoT from batch 2; per-batch numbers appear only in Fig 4.
results.quote: the superiority of GeM-CoT gets prominent from batch 2

limits: Authors concede it does not improve the reasoning process itself; existing reasoning improvements could be layered on.
Authors concede more efficient demo selection in mixed-task scenarios is left open.
Wrong type matches can derail reasoning (App E.2, StrategyQA examples).
Single runs, no variance or seeds; only OpenAI models at temperature 1.0; code and prompts not released in text.
Mixed-task benchmark is a shuffle of public datasets with a pre-built demo pool from Wei et al. data; the 10 datasets seed the pool so are not unseen.

terms.definition: the type of any incoming question is unknown; the input data comes from a set of mixed tasks; the questions come in an arbitrary order
